Detailed Description

A BinaryOpUGen usually created using the function ring1() when applied to other UGen instances.

It is not normally required to use this UGen explicitly. 

 UGen resultRing1  = SinOsc::AR(100, 0, 0.4).ring1(SinOsc::AR(400, 0, 0.3)); // creates a BinaryRing1UGen

You can also use a global version of this function, the above code would be equivalent as: 

 UGen resultRing1  =  ring1(SinOsc::AR(100, 0, 0.4), SinOsc::AR(400, 0, 0.3)); // creates a BinaryRing1UGen
See also:
